rv.q: Walker's play is a gripping, fresh and pleasingly twisted romance.
An urgent, contemporary play that uses the limitations of a fringe venue to amplify its characters and its emotions.

Burnt-Up Love looks at physical and emotional damage travelling down generations; it takes a good swipe at the prison system and at alpha males; it mingles warning and hope. It is a glimpse rather than a full drama, often describing rather than showing its considerable action; but the description is crisp, and the result ferocious.
It is a very powerful, involving, piece of writing and stagecraft, and needs to be seen – highly recommended!

He knows of her through an old photo adorning his cell wall and this imagined reality keeps him motivated. Joanne Marie Mason plays Scratch with a sustained vocal and physical energy that excites and repels in equal measure. It is a dynamic performance, drawing us into her chaotic world.
